newsitem.title: INDIA: India says US trade move at odds with growing ties.
newsitem.headline: India says US trade move at odds with growing ties.

text.p: India said on Thursday it regretted a U.S. decision to keep it on a "watch list" of countries potentially subject to trade sanctions for alleged failure to protect intellectual property rights.

The Foreign Ministry said in a statement the U.S. decision to keep India on its "Special 301" list was not "in consonance with the positive trend in the development of commercial and business relations between India and the United States".
"The Government of India notes with regret the decision of the U.S. Government to continue to place India on the priority watch list under their 'Special 301' provisions," the statement said.
The U.S. Trade Representative's Office on Wednesday released its Special 301 annual review of how countries protect copyrights and other intellectual property from piracy.
A nation judged to have a persistently poor record could be subject to U.S. trade sanctions.
Washington cited India among countries it said would be closely watched to see if they abided by obligations to protect copyrights from piracy.
Indian officials said Washington had taken aim at New Delhi's alleged failure to protect patents on pharmaceuticals and agricultural chemicals.
The ministry said both countries were members of the World Trade Organisation, which it said provided the appropriate forum for discussing and resolving such matters.

Growing cooperation in trade and economic matters in recent years demonstrated U.S. companies "have a keen appreciation of the rights and safeguards provided under the administrative, legal and judicial processes in India", it said.
The United States is India's biggest trading and investment partner.
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) said the U.S. move "was clearly aimed at pressurising India to offer greater trade concessions".
The CII said the U.S. decision to keep India on the priority watch list was uncalled for as New Delhi had not rejected intellectual property safeguards or any patent applications.
"This unilateral move was against the spirit embodied in the World Trade Organisation," it said.
The CII said the Indian government had told U.S. officials last year that it would like to push a patents protection bill through parliament, but an exact time frame could not be guaranteed.
